hypotheses.title: Large-Cap Asset Fair Value Growth and Operating Earnings Yield Divergence
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Companies with high asset fair value (fn_assets_fair_val_a) relative to trailing domestic (fnd2_ebitdm) and foreign (fnd2_ebitfr) operating earnings represent firms that have aggressively invested in productive capacity that has not yet reached peak earnings maturity. In sizable large-cap equities (TOP1000/TOP500), high asset fair value relative to market price and operating earnings signifies asset backing and future expansion rather than financial distress. By incorporating subindustry neutralization, quadratic power conviction, and short-term price reversal stabilizers, we isolate intra-industry capital maturation alpha.
hypotheses.falsification_test: Alpha fails if high asset fair value stems from stranded or overvalued legacy assets that never generate operational cash flows.

candidates.expression: 0.85 * signed_power(group_rank((group_rank(fn_assets_fair_val_a, subindustry) > 0.5 ? 2.0 : 1.0) * (-group_rank(fnd2_ebitdm, subindustry) - group_rank(fnd2_ebitfr, subindustry)), subindustry) - 0.5, 2) - 0.15 * group_rank(ts_delta(close, 3) / close, subindustry)
candidates.rationale: Candidate 1: Subindustry-neutralized Alpha 5 compound blueprint applied to prompt's conditional asset-to-EBIT signal with 15% 3-day reversal stabilizer
Candidate 2: Continuous division-safe operating earning power per unit of asset fair value with 15% 3-day reversal stabilizer
Candidate 3: 1-year time-series fair value asset yield trajectory (Alpha 8/9 architecture)
